modality_preference.survey_note: Ground Truth Solutions Cash Barometer, Apr 2024: face-to-face survey of 1,952 people (Borno 1,268, Yobe 684), 18 Oct-2 Nov 2023; text says people generally prefer vouchers to unrestricted cash; 42% (Borno) and 17% (Yobe) favoured mixed food and cash. Adamawa excluded. [s6] 2026 HNRP foreword reportedly says communities prefer cash (via gDCF analysis; not verified). HNRP 2026: 92% of surveyed beneficiaries prefer cash (likely PDM of cash recipients; sample not stated). GTS Cash Barometer 2024 (Borno, Yobe) found people generally prefer vouchers to unrestricted cash — the two findings conflict and come from different populations.

ai_summary.headline: Nigeria has a mature cash architecture, but MPC is small and the plan's headline cash figures need correcting.
ai_summary.narrative: The 2026 HNRP seeks $516.4m for 2.5m people in the BAY states, and FTS shows $367.7m received as of this pull, about 71% [s1][s2]. Over a third of that is not assigned to a cluster, so coverage is likely overstated for sector analysis. Multi-Purpose Cash has received $6.7m, 1.8% of funding, but FTS carries no 2026 MPC requirement, so coverage cannot be judged [s2]. The gDCF analysis quotes $255m CVA and $15m MPC against a $910m plan; the denominator is the 2025 figure, so those numbers should be treated as unverified. Coordination is strong: a national CWG co-led by OCHA and the federal ministry, a north-east group co-chaired with CRS, 132 members, and a JMMI with a round in December 2025 [s4][s5][s7]. The national CVA policy and social registry give a social-protection route [s4]. Preference evidence is dated: GTS found people generally favour vouchers over unrestricted cash in Borno and Yobe in 2023 [s6].
